key_insight: With the same preoperative variables, newer machine-learning architectures only slightly improved perioperative risk prediction over logistic regression.
clinical_relevance: For perioperative planning, model choice mattered less than the fixed predictor set, and an established surgical risk calculator performed similarly for mortality but worse for complications.
method: Trained six tabular model families and three pretrained clinical text-encoder classifiers using 73 prespecified preoperative variables.
Used 4,995,670 ACS NSQIP cases from 2018-2022 for training and 963,565 cases from 2024 for temporal testing.
Compared performance across four 30-day outcomes using AUROC and checked results in a 3,490-case single-institution deployment set.
evidence_signal: On temporal testing, the FT-Transformer was best or tied best for all four outcomes (AUROC 0.755-0.955), but its advantage over logistic regression was only 0.009-0.030 and the text encoders were within 0.005-0.009 of the top tabular model.
watch_item: Performance rankings changed under AUPRC and did not consistently hold in the small single-institution deployment check, so local validation remains important.
paper_title: From National Data to Local Evaluation: Benchmarking Machine Learning Models for Perioperative Risk Prediction
